message.content:
In Blackjack, an Ace is a “flexible” card because it can be worth either **1 point** or **11 points**, depending on which value gives your hand the best chance of winning without going over 21.  

- If counting the Ace as 11 keeps your total ≤ 21, it’s treated as 11.  
- If counting it as 11 would make you bust (> 21), it’s automatically counted as 1.  

This dual‑value nature makes hands containing an Ace “soft” (e.g., Ace‑7 is a soft 18). If you have two Aces, one will usually count as 11 and the other as 1, giving you a soft 12. The dealer follows the same rule when deciding whether to hit or stand.
